# External torsion phases and divisibility in the field generated by the seed

<a id="finding"></a>
## Independent whole-proof review

At 2026-11-21T05:44 UTC an agent working for Sheng Yin independently reviewed the full [C345 v771](../../claims/Yin_C_G0345_v771.md#statement) and recommends acceptance.
The reviewer received the fixed claim and the requested topics of inspection, without participating in its development or consulting a previous verdict.

For a positive common multiple \(B\) of the orders of the torsion quotients of conjugates of \(\beta\) by \(\beta\), the stabilizer of \(\beta^B\) consists precisely of the automorphisms fixing the class \(f=[\beta]\).
An automorphism fixing a representative of a nonzero rational multiple of \(f\) fixes \(f\), by unique divisibility modulo torsion.
This gives the stated field containment, including for representatives whose translating phase lies outside \(F\).
The intersection of the rational line with the classes represented in each fixed field is discrete by Northcott applied with bounded height and fixed degree.
In \(F\) the corresponding subgroup of \(\mathbb Q\) contains \(1\), hence equals \((1/k_F)\mathbb Z\), where exactly the divisors of \(k_F\) are admissible integral root exponents modulo its torsion group.

In \(K\) the normalized generator satisfies \(bf=a[u]\) with \(a,b\) coprime.
The fraction \(p/q=(a/\gcd(a,g))/(bg/\gcd(a,g))\) is in lowest terms.
Every \(K\)-embedding of \(\mathbb Q(\alpha)\) fixes \([\alpha]=(p/q)[u]\), so the relative norm represents \(tp[u]/q\) in \(K\).
The generator property forces \(q\mid t\).
A root of \(X^q-u^p\) has this same class, hence its field contains \(K\), and its relative degree is at most \(q\).
It attains degree \(q\) and satisfies the allowed translated equation because its class is \(f/g\).
Thus the minimal measure ratio is \(q/(\kappa g)=1/(e\gcd(a,g))\), and every ratio is a positive integer multiple.
The minimum-degree formula itself agrees with Proposition 3.2 of Fili and Miner with \(\ell=b\) and \(n=a\).
The selected text on pages 19–22 also uses the relative norm for the matched lower bound and a binomial for attainment.

The element \(\xi=\beta^b/u^a\) belongs to \(\mu(F)\) and \([F:K(\xi)]\le b\).
Combining the tower with the integral divisibility \(b\mid\kappa\) gives \(1\le e\le[K(\xi):K]\le\varphi(w)\), since the order of \(\xi\) divides \(w\).
The Bézout product \(\beta^iu^j\) represents \(f/a\) in \(F\).
The norm of an \(F\)-representative of \(f/k_F\) represents \((ae/k_F)[u]\) in \(K\), so \(a\mid k_F\mid ae\).
It follows that (2) holds for all external phases and that \(\mu(F)\subset K\) suffices for \(e=1\) and \(a=k_F\).
This includes totally imaginary fields with torsion group \(\{\pm1\}\).
In the sign case a witness \(\theta^{k_F}=\pm\beta\) in \(F\) generates \(F\) over \(\mathbb Q\), because its power generates \(F\).
Substitution of \(\pm X\) preserves the coefficient length of an annihilator, so the [ordinary denominator theorem](../../claims/Yin_C_G0345_v210.md#statement) applies with relative degree one and yields \(k_F\mid R_L\).
For general bounded-length units the [saturation bound](../../claims/Yin_C_G0345_v767.md#statement) at a witness gives \(k_F\le H_Lw\).
If the seed measures stay above a fixed positive value and the translated measures tend to zero, every bounded subsequence of \(w\) would violate (3).
For a nonunit seed the translated radical remains a nonunit at a finite place, and a leading or constant coefficient of its primitive minimal polynomial then has absolute value at least two.

For real \(y\ne0\), set \(K'=\mathbb Q(y^n)\) where \(n\) is the order of the proposed multiplier.
Over \(K'\) each conjugate of \(y\) or of \(\zeta y\) is \(y\) times an \(n\)-th root of unity.
Their field norm over \(K'\) is \(y^t\) times a sign, since it lies in the chosen real field and \(y\) is real.
The exponents with \(y^s\in K'\) form a subgroup of \(\mathbb Z\), so its positive generator divides both relative degrees.
For \(y\) itself the binomial of that degree over \(K'\) gives the reverse bound, proving divisibility of absolute degrees and minimality of the positive branch.
In the example with \(u=(1+\sqrt5)/2\) and \(\zeta\) of order three, \(\beta^3=2u+1\) recovers \(u\) and then \(\zeta=\beta/u\).
The real quadratic field and the imaginary quadratic cyclotomic field have compositum degree four.
For the two conjugates \(u,u'\), multiplication of \(X^2+uX+u^2\) and \(X^2+u'X+u'^2\) gives precisely the displayed quartic of coefficient length six.
The height invariance under \(\zeta\) gives the ratio \(1/2\) at \(g=1\).
